overview: Black adopts a Caro-Kann/Modern hybrid: ...g6, ...Bg7, ...c6 and ...d5 against White's big centre of e4, d4, f4. After 5.e5 Black plays ...h5, hitting g4 and preparing ...Bg4, ...Nh6 and ...Nf5. White gets space and a Pirc-like attack set-up, but must care for the e5 pawn and the d4 point.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the space with e5/f4 and develop Nf3, Be2 or Bd3
Play Be3, Qd2 and h3 to restrict Black's pieces
Aim for a kingside attack or a Nb5 jump

black_ideas.idea: Prepare ...Bg4 and trade pieces to relieve the space deficit
Hit the chain base with ...f6 or ...Nh6-f5
Use the ...h5-h4 pawn to unsettle White's kingside

typical_structures.structure: French Advance-like chain e5/d4 with an extra f4 pawn
Black bishop on g7 hemmed in until ...f6

character.notes: A cramped but resilient Black set-up against a big White centre, with both sides ready to push on the kingside.

structure.notes: The e5/d4/f4 chain against ...c6/...d5 locks the centre.

approach.notes: A rare move-order trick, used by few strong players.

level.notes: Needs to understand how to meet the space advantage rather than memorise.

sublines_that_differ.name: Caro-Kann transposition
sublines_that_differ.how: The most played route; same position reached via Caro-Kann.

character.reason: White's big centre and Black's ...h5 lunge create mutual kingside risks.

gambit.reason: Material is level and no pawn is offered.

soundness.reason: A rare but playable Black set-up.

structure.reason: The e5, d4 and f4 chain faces ...c6 and ...d5 in a locked centre.

approach.reason: Played by few strong players, mainly as a surprise.

level.reason: Plans are fairly clear but Black must handle the cramped position with care.

plans.reason: White holds a clear space advantage and Black's g7-bishop is blocked.
